To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL12RB1 is a novel example of a human cytokine gene that is posttranscriptionally edited to generate a diverse mRNA repertoire.

IL12RB1 is an example of an immune receptor that is subject to posttranscriptional RNA-DNA editing and that this editing is a novel mechanism that contributes to interindividual variation in IL12/12R1 sensitivity.

the interleukin-23 receptor (IL23R) mRNA repertoire in primary human immune cells contains a number of RNA–DNA differences (RDDs), which are introduced posttransciptonally, and that these differences negatively regulate IL23R’s binding of its ligand IL23.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the human interleukin (IL)-12 receptor β1 gene (IL12RB 1), which regulates the susceptibility or resistance to mycobacterial infection and other human diseases.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of individual differences in susceptibility to human disease.
the mechanisms that underlie individual differences in immune responses to mycobacterial infections
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the introduction of RNA-Dna differences underlies inter-individual variation in the human Interleukin 12 receptor beta 1 mRNA repertoire.

the introduction of posttranscriptional RNA-DNA differences into the IL12RB1 transcriptome is a novel mechanism that regulates IL12/23 signaling and may contribute to interindividual differences in IL12Rβ’s binding of IL-12 and/or IL-23.

the introduction of RNA-Dna differences (RDDs), a mechanism of post-transcriptional diversification, into the human interleukin 1 receptor beta 1 (IL1RB1) transcriptome, underlies individual differences in IL1R1 function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the introduction of RNA-Dna differences (RDDs), a mechanism of sequence diversity, into the IL12Rβ mRNAs of human immune cells underlies individual differences in IL-12/IL-23 sensitivity.
the introduction of RNA-Dna Differences (RDDs) into the IL12RB1 RNA repertoire underlies interindividual variability in the human IL-12/23 sensitivity and susceptibility to mycobacterial infection.
the introduction of RNA-DNAdifferences into IL12RB mRNAs in primary cells underlies interindividual differences in the human IL-12Rβ1 mRNA repertoire.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL12RB1 is an example of a human cytokine that is subject to posttranscriptional sequence diversification.

the introduction of RNA-Dna differences (RDDs), which are nucleotide differences that occur posttranscriptionally between RNA and its DNA template, into IL12RB mRNAs negatively regulate IL12RB1 binding to its cytokine ligand, IL-12p40.
the introduction of RNA-Dna Differences underlies individual differences in IL-12/23 sensitivity, which is important for the development of mycobacterial disease.
